en: I can leave out what does not need saying: I would if I could, so do I, the former and the latter.
I can push the weight to the end and carry the stress to the front: Into the hall came and What he did next was.
I can choose the fixed forms of formal request: I insist that he be, were it not for and lest.
I can set the tone of concession and contrast: granted, albeit, whereas and much as I.
I can use settled collocations and light verbs: take issue with, bear the brunt, draw a distinction.
I can say the same content in three registers: legal language, neutral language and spoken language.
I can load the judgement onto the reporting verb: he claimed, he conceded, he alleged.
I can set the distance with modal nuance: may well, might have been expected to, would tend to.
I can build and hear understatement and irony: not exactly cheap, I wouldn't say no.
I can hold a whole text together: this, such, the latter and signposts at paragraph level.
